title: Days of making (Genesis 1:6–25)
hookLine: sky, sea, land, plants, stars, fish, birds, animals, and after each: it was good

lines: A CARPENTER STEPS BACK AND NODS.
GOD MAKES, AND THEN GOD LOOKS.
cards: A carpenter steps back from a cabinet, runs a hand along the edge, and nods. A gardener looks down a row of seedlings, every one of them up. A kid holds up a drawing, still wet.
That small pause, when someone makes a thing and then looks at it, runs all through the first chapter of the Bible.

Day by day, the empty world fills: sky, sea, dry land, green things, lights, swimmers, fliers, creatures that creep and run. And after the making, again and again, God looks, and the same short sentence comes back.

teach.b: Read the chapter slowly and a shape appears. The first three days make spaces. Day one, light and dark.

Day two, a firmament, a great dome that splits the waters above from the waters below, and God calls it heaven. Day three, the waters gather, dry land appears, and the land brings forth grass and trees with seed in them.
The next three days fill those spaces. Day four fills day and night with lights: "the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also."
The sun and moon aren't even named, just lights, with a job. Day five fills the sea and sky with fish and birds. Day six fills the land with animals, and with people, which is tomorrow.
And after the making comes the line: "and God saw that it was good."

teach.h: TOV: GOOD, LIKE A GOOD MEAL.
teach.b: In Hebrew, good is tov, the same word you'd use for a good meal or a good day.
A small surprise: day two, the dome in the sky, is the one day where the Hebrew text doesn't say it was good. Readers have offered reasons; nobody knows for sure.

teach.h: AND GOD SAW THAT IT WAS GOOD.
teach.b: Count the goods through the whole chapter, including the very good on day six, and you get seven. Christians read the days differently, some as six literal days, others as a poem with a pattern.
Either way, the refrain is there to hear. Before anyone did anything right or wrong, the world was called good.

how: Some churches use the refrain of Genesis 1 in thanksgiving and creation-care services, and some keep a Season of Creation each September with readings from this chapter.

o: perfect, with no flaw anywhere at all
good, as in a good meal or a good day
holy, set apart only for God's use

games.q: which day of making — tap the pairs.

s: Genesis 1 names the sun and the moon on day four
it calls them the greater light and the lesser light, with a job: to rule the day and the night.
in the Hebrew text, day two doesn't say it was good
the dome in the sky is the one day without the refrain. nobody knows for sure why.
the first three days make spaces and the next three fill them
light, sky and sea, land; then lights, fish and birds, animals and people.

games.q: you've just made the dry land and the trees with seed in them. what comes next in the story?
o: you look at it, and call it good.
games.why: "and God saw that it was good." the pause after the making comes again and again, before anyone has done anything right or wrong.

practice: Find one thing from the sky or the water, like a cloud or a glass of water; one green thing; and one living creature, a dog, a pigeon, a person you can hear in the next room.
For each, pause the way the story does, look at it properly, and say quietly, it is good. If you pray, you can give thanks for each.

wordCard.voice: Tov. The Hebrew word for good, the refrain after each day of making: the same good used for a good meal.

orig.note: Hebrew: good, the everyday word for a good meal or a good day, and the refrain of Genesis 1.

carryVoice: Your line: and it was good. Seven times in one chapter, the same short sentence. See you tomorrow.
